58911-autographs-for-freedom.title: Autographs For Freedom
58911-autographs-for-freedom.creator: Unknown
58911-autographs-for-freedom.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. and, the great sin of SLAVERY. Should this publication be instrumental in casting _one_ ray of hope on the heart of one poor slave, or should it draw the attention of one person, hitherto uninterested, to the deep wrongs of the bondman, or cause one sincere and earnest effort to promote emancipation, we believe that the kind contributors, who have generously responded to our call, not less than the members of our Society, will feel themselves gratified and compensated.

arxiv-2005-11168.title: QuIS: The Question of Intelligent Site Selection
arxiv-2005-11168.creator: Sebastian Baumbach, Florian Sachs, Sheraz Ahmed, Andreas Dengel
arxiv-2005-11168.description: Abstract Site selection is one of the most important decisions to be made by companies. Such a decision depends on various factors of sites, including socio-economic, geographical, ecological, as well as specific requirements of companies. The existing approaches for site selection are manual, subjective, and not scalable.

arxiv-2104-13715.title: PyTorchDIA: A flexible, GPU-accelerated numerical approach to Difference Image Analysis 2020 PyTorchDIA: A flexible, GPU-accelerated numerical approach to Difference Image Analysis – References
arxiv-2104-13715.creator: James A. Hitchcock, Markus Hundertmark, Daniel Foreman-Mackey, Etienne Bachelet, Martin Dominik, Rachel Street, Yiannis Tsapras
arxiv-2104-13715.description: Abstract We present a GPU-accelerated numerical approach for fast kernel and differential background solutions. The model image proposed in the Bramich (2008) difference image analysis algorithm is analogous to a very simple Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), with a single convolutional filter (i.e. the kernel) and an added scalar bias (i.e. the differential background).

arxiv-2106-03424.title: Axion-Like Particle Searches with IACTs
arxiv-2106-03424.creator: Ivana Batković, Alessandro De Angelis, Michele Doro, Marina Manganaro
arxiv-2106-03424.description: Abstract The growing interest in axion-like particles (ALPs) stems from the fact that they provide successful theoretical explanations of physics phenomena, from the anomaly of the C ​ P CP -symmetry conservation in strong interactions to the observation of an unexpectedly large TeV photon flux from astrophysical sources, at distances where the strong absorption by the intergalactic medium should make

arxiv-2204-05113.title: ShiftNAS: Towards Automatic Generation of Advanced Mulitplication-Less Neural Networks
arxiv-2204-05113.creator: Xiaoxuan Lou, Guowen Xu, Kangjie Chen, Guanlin Li, Jiwei Li, Tianwei Zhang
arxiv-2204-05113.description: Abstract Multiplication-less neural networks significantly reduce the time and energy cost on the hardware platform, as the compute-intensive multiplications are replaced with lightweight bit-shift operations. However, existing bit-shift networks are all directly transferred from state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which lead to non-negligible accuracy drop or even failure of model convergence.

arxiv-2205-12152.title: Performance Analysis of Downlink MIMO-NOMA Systems Over Weibull Fading Channels Thanks: The work of L. P. J. Jiménez was supported by Eldorado Research Institute. The work of F. D. A. García was supported by the São Paulo Research Foundation (FAPESP) under Grant 2021/03923-9.
arxiv-2205-12152.creator: Lenin Patricio Jiménez Jiménez, Fernando Darío Almeida García, Maria Cecilia Luna Alvarado, Gustavo Fraidenraich, Michel Daoud Yacoub, José Cândido S. Santos Filho, Eduardo Rodrigues de Lima
arxiv-2205-12152.description: Abstract This work analyzes the performance of a downlink multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) communications system. To reduce hardware complexity and exploit antenna diversity, we consider a transmit antenna selection (TAS) scheme and equal-gain combining (EGC) receivers.

arxiv-2206-05285.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Hoang Le Truong, Hoang Ngoc Yen. In this paper, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of Ulrich bundles on cubic fourfold X X of given rank r r . As consequences, we show that for every integer r ≥ 2 r\geq 2 there exists a family of indecomposable rank r r Ulrich bundles on the certain cubic fourfolds, depending roughly on r r parameters, and in particular they are of wild representation type; special surfaces on the cubic fourfolds are explicitly

arxiv-2211-02565.title: Coherent and incoherent structures in fuzzy dark matter halos 2022 Coherent and incoherent structures in fuzzy dark matter halos –
arxiv-2211-02565.creator: I-Kang Liu, Nick P. Proukakis, Gerasimos Rigopoulos
arxiv-2211-02565.description: Abstract We show that fuzzy dark matter halos exhibit spatial differentiation in the coherence of the field configuration, ranging from completely coherent in the central solitonic core to incoherent outside it, with a significant drop of the dimensionless phase-space density with increasing radius.

arxiv-2302-04117.title: A polyhedral homotopy algorithm for computing critical points of polynomial programs
arxiv-2302-04117.creator: Julia Lindberg, Leonid Monin, Kemal Rose
arxiv-2302-04117.description: Abstract . In this paper we propose a method that uses Lagrange multipliers and numerical algebraic geometry to find all critical points, and therefore globally solve, polynomial optimization problems. We design a polyhedral homotopy algorithm that explicitly constructs an optimal start system, circumventing the typical bottleneck associated with polyhedral homotopy algorithms.

arxiv-2405-12503.title: CLRKDNet: Speeding up Lane Detection with Knowledge Distillation
arxiv-2405-12503.creator: Weiqing Qi, Guoyang Zhao, Fulong Ma, Linwei Zheng, Ming Liu
arxiv-2405-12503.description: Abstract Road lanes are integral components of the visual perception systems in intelligent vehicles, playing a pivotal role in safe navigation. In lane detection tasks, balancing accuracy with real-time performance is essential, yet existing methods often sacrifice one for the other. To address this trade-off, we introduce CLRKDNet, a streamlined model that balances detection accuracy with real-time performance.

arxiv-2409-04841.title: Hölder regularity for nonlocal in time subdiffusion equations with general kernel
arxiv-2409-04841.description: Abstract We study the regularity of weak solutions to nonlocal in time subdiffusion equations for a wide class of weakly singular kernels appearing in the generalised fractional derivative operator. We prove a weak Harnack inequality for nonnegative weak supersolutions and Hölder continuity of weak solutions to such problems.

arxiv-2502-00780.title: Constructing Fundamentals for the Theory of Proportions and Symbolic Allusions Applied Interdisciplinarily
arxiv-2502-00780.creator: Diogen Babuc
arxiv-2502-00780.description: Abstract . The Theory of Proportions and Symbolic Allusions Applied Interdisciplinary (TPASAI) is a framework that integrates mathematics, linguistics, psychology, and game theory to uncover hidden patterns and proportions in reality. Its central idea is that numerical encoding of symbols, dates, and language can reveal recurring structures and connections that reflect universal principles.

arxiv-2502-01765.title: Tracking the Chemical Evolution of Hydrocarbons Through Carbon Grain Supply in Protoplanetary Disks
arxiv-2502-01765.creator: Eshan Raul, Felipe Alarcón, Edwin A. Bergin
arxiv-2502-01765.description: Abstract The gas present in planet-forming disks typically exhibits strong emission features of abundant carbon and oxygen molecular carriers. In some instances, protoplanetary disks show an elevated C/O ratio above interstellar values, which leads to a rich hydrocarbon chemistry evidenced in the mid-infrared spectra.

arxiv-2502-18774.title: Measuring risks inherent to our digital economies using Amazon purchase histories from US consumers
arxiv-2502-18774.creator: Alex Berke, Kent Larson, Sandy Pentland, Dana Calacci
arxiv-2502-18774.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alex Berke, Kent Larson, Sandy Pentland, Dana Calacci. What do pickles and trampolines have in common? In this paper we show that while purchases for these products may seem innocuous, they risk revealing clues about customers’ personal attributes — in this case, their race. As online retail and digital purchases become increasingly common, consumer data has become increasingly valuable, raising the risks of privacy violations and online discrimination.

arxiv-2510-11307.title: FOSSIL: Harnessing Feedback on Suboptimal Samples for Data-Efficient Generalisation with Imitation Learning for Embodied Vision-and-Language Tasks
arxiv-2510-11307.creator: Sabrina McCallum, Amit Parekh, Alessandro Suglia
arxiv-2510-11307.description: Abstract Current approaches to embodied AI tend to learn policies from expert demonstrations. However, without a mechanism to evaluate the quality of demonstrated actions, they are limited to learning from optimal behaviour, or they risk replicating errors and inefficiencies. While reinforcement learning offers one alternative, the associated exploration typically results in sacrificing data efficiency.

arxiv-2512-04534.title: Refaçade: Editing Object with Given Reference Texture
arxiv-2512-04534.creator: Youze Huang, Penghui Ruan, Bojia Zi, Xianbiao Qi, Jianan Wang, Rong Xiao
arxiv-2512-04534.description: Abstract Recent advances in diffusion models have brought remarkable progress in image and video editing, yet some tasks remain underexplored. In this paper, we introduce a new task, Object Retexture , which transfers local textures from a reference object to a target object in images or videos.

arxiv-2602-22813.title: Input–Envelope–Output: Auditable Generative Music Rewards in Sensory-Sensitive Contexts Conference: Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Sys
arxiv-2602-22813.creator: Cong Ye, Songlin Shang, Xiaoxu Ma, Xiangbo Zhang
arxiv-2602-22813.description: Abstract . Generative feedback in sensory-sensitive contexts poses a core design challenge: large individual differences in sensory tolerance make it difficult to sustain engagement without compromising safety. This tension is exemplified in autism spectrum disorder (ASD), where auditory sensitivities are common yet highly heterogeneous.

plos-pone-0004589.creator: Wessel M. A. van Leeuwen, Maili Lehto, Piia Karisola et al.
plos-pone-0004589.description: PLOS ONE research article. Sleep restriction, leading to deprivation of sleep, is common in modern 24-h societies and is associated with the development of health problems including cardiovascular diseases. Our objective was to investigate the immunological effects of prolonged sleep restriction and subseq

pmc-10738424.title: IDENTIFYING NEW ADRD DIAGNOSES IN HOME HEALTH CARE PATIENTS USING NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING OF NURSES’ NOTES
pmc-10738424.creator: Yolanda Barrón, Miriam Ryvicker, Jiyoun Song, Maryam Zolnoori, Maxim Topaz
pmc-10738424.description: Patients at risk of developing Alzheimer’s Disease and Related Dementias (ADRD) admitted to home health care (HHC) may show signs of the disease before receiving a formal diagnosis. HHC nurses are uniquely positioned to observe signs of patients’ cognitive symptoms and may record them in free-text notes in the electronic health record (EHR).

pmc-11331413.title: Conformational dynamics of the hepatitis C virus 3′X RNA
pmc-11331413.creator: Parker D. Sperstad, Erik D. Holmstrom
pmc-11331413.description: The 3′ end of the hepatitis C virus genome is terminated by a highly conserved, 98 nt sequence called 3′X. This untranslated structural element is thought to regulate several essential RNA-dependent processes associated with infection. 3′X has two proposed conformations comprised of either three or two stem–loop structures that result from the different base-pairing interactions within the first 55 nt.

pmc-11371646.title: Fc-engineered antibodies promote neutrophil-dependent control of Mycobacterium tuberculosis
pmc-11371646.creator: Edward B. Irvine, Angel Nikolov, Mehak Z. Khan, Joshua M. Peters, Richard Lu, Jaimie Sixsmith, Aaron Wallace, Esther van Woudenbergh, Sally Shin, Wiktor Karpinski, Jeff C. Hsiao, Arturo Casadevall, Bryan D. Bryson, Lisa Cavacini, Patricia S. Grace, Galit Alter, Sarah M. Fortune
pmc-11371646.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Mounting evidence indicates that antibodies can contribute towards control of tuberculosis (TB). However, the underlying mechanisms of humoral immune protection and whether antibodies can be exploited in therapeutic strategies to combat TB are relatively understudied. Here we engineered the receptor-binding Fc (fragment crystallizable) region of an antibody recognizing the Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) capsule, to define antibody Fc-mediated mechanism(s) of Mtb restriction.

pmc-11691823.title: THE ROLE OF SOCIODEMOGRAPHIC FACTORS IN COMMUNITY-BASED REHABILITATION USE AFTER HIP ARTHROPLASTY
pmc-11691823.creator: Allyn Bove, Christopher Bise, Lauren Terhorst, Kelli Allen, Jared Magnani, Anthony Delitto, Janet Freburger
pmc-11691823.description: Community-based rehabilitation in the home health and outpatient settings is an important element of recovering function after total hip arthroplasty (THA). While there is ample evidence confirming sociodemographic differences in THA rates and short-term outcomes (e.g., post-operative complications), it is unclear whether there are differences in use of rehabilitation after THA.

pmc-12428457.title: The Role of Vascularization in Nerve Regeneration: Mechanistic and Therapeutic Perspectives
pmc-12428457.creator: Hamid Malekzadeh, Reade Otto-Moudry, Amy M. Moore
pmc-12428457.description: Peripheral nerve injuries (PNIs) are common and often result in sensorimotor deficits, chronic pain and decreased quality of life. While the peripheral nervous system has greater regenerative capacity than the central nervous system, recovery is often limited by intrinsic changes in the nerve and muscle.

pmc-13188299.title: The prognostic significance of the mechanism of mild to moderate alkalemia at emergency department admission
pmc-13188299.creator: Ivan Gur, Amichai Gutgold, Asaf Miller
pmc-13188299.description: BackgroundPaucity of evidence exists as to the prognostic significance of mild to moderate alkalemia upon presentation to the emergency department (ED).MethodsPatients presenting to the ED of one tertiary hospital over the last 24 years were included in this retrospective cohort study if the serum pH drawn within 3 h of the initial presentation was 7.45–7.55.

pmc-13254901.title: Tumor infiltrating B cells and tertiary lymphoid structures in pancreatic cancer prognosis and therapy
pmc-13254901.creator: Zichen Pan, Fusheng Zhang, Cuixia Zhang, Xingyue Li, Yongsu Ma, Yinmo Yang, Xiaodong Tian
pmc-13254901.description: SummaryPancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, characterized by a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that limits response to immunotherapy. Tumor-infiltrating B cells (TIBs) constitute a key TME component, and in certain patient subsets, they collaborate with T cells, dendritic cells, and other immune cells to form tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs).

pmc-13480047.title: Antenatal intervention for childbirth trauma: the clinical profile of Australian women at a tertiary hospital
pmc-13480047.creator: Kelli K MacMillan, Catherine F Greenhalgh, Dominique B Cleary, Jacqueline Cahill, Kellie Dedman, Chloe Weir, Carolyn Bright, Scott W White, Zoe Bradfield, Stuart J Watson

pmc-13560103.title: Critical Review on the Development and Evolution of Beat Perception
pmc-13560103.creator: Gábor Háden, Henkjan Honing
pmc-13560103.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Beat perception—the ability to extract a regular pulse from rhythmic sequences—is a foundational component of human musicality and a key mechanism supporting synchronization, dance, and collective music‐making. Research across neuroscience, developmental psychology, and comparative cognition demonstrates that beat processing exhibits four defining characteristics: it is near‐universal across human cultures, emerges spontaneously in early development, engages domain‐specific predictive timing mechanisms, and appears rare across species.
